key_insight: This paper introduces the self-building laboratory (SBL): an AI-driven lab that can design, configure, and operate its own experimental setup instead of being limited to pre-built procedures. The key breakthrough is making lab infrastructure adaptable, so automation can scale beyond a fixed menu of experiments.
problem_solved: Current self-driving laboratories can automate experiments, but only for procedures they were explicitly engineered to run. When a new experiment is needed, extensive manual lab reconfiguration becomes the bottleneck, slowing scientific discovery and limiting flexibility.
method: Uses AI agents to plan new experiments and determine the required lab setup.
Automatically designs and configures laboratory components to match the target procedure.
Integrates building, setup, and operation into a closed-loop system for more flexible experimentation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this points toward a more general and scalable automation stack where agents are not just experiment planners but also infrastructure builders. It could greatly reduce the engineering overhead of adapting laboratories to new research tasks.
